subject: MAP: technical evaluation slate & milestone alignment
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.inference>
To: Caroline Park <caroline.park@healthgrid.com>, Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@healthgrid.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP: technical evaluation slate & milestone alignment

Thanks again for a productive call earlier, Caroline and Alex — appreciate you walking through the high-level goals for HealthGrid's clinical summarization pilot. Per the MAP we discussed, I put together a first-pass technical evaluation slate and a proposed milestone schedule so we can align on owners and blockers. Key asks at this stage:

- Confirm owners for benchmarks and infra (see proposed owners below).
- Agree on latency and cost SLOs that represent production-like traffic.
- Validate the model shortlist satisfies PHI-handling and quantization objectives.

Attached: MAP-draft-v1.pdf (MAP with milestones), latency-cost-targets.xlsx, model-shortlist.csv

High-level milestones (proposed):
1) Dataset & access (HealthGrid to provide sanitized dataset extract) — target owner: Alex Mercer — due 2026-10-26
2) Baseline run (open-model slate + Redwood default config) — owner: Diego Fernandez — due 2026-11-02
3) Latency/cost bench & tuning pass — owner: Karthik Iyer — due 2026-11-09
4) Quality eval + guardrails check (PHI removal, hallucination rate) — owner: HealthGrid QA (Caroline) + Redwood SEs — due 2026-11-16
5) Acceptance decision & production rollout plan — owner: HealthGrid PM + Redwood AM — target close: 2026-11-30

Bench success criteria (draft):
- ROUGE-L improvement over baseline >= 6 pts OR clinician pass-rate >= 88% on clinical sanity checks
- 95th percentile response latency <= 250ms (for 256-token output)
- Average per-1k-token cost <= $0.85 (Redwood-configured execution)

Model shortlist notes (attached CSV): preference for quantized FP16/INT8 variants with known PHI-safe pretraining; candidates: OpenMed-7B, MedT5-3B, RW-Instruct-13B (quantized), and a smaller trial with OpenLlama-3B for cost baseline.

Next steps: if this slate looks acceptable, can you confirm dataset access timing and whether Procurement needs any extra artifacts to start the contract path?

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.inference
+1 (415) 555-0192

Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: technical evaluation slate & milestone alignment

Vanessa — thanks, this is helpful. Quick answers:
- Dataset: we can provide a de-identified extract by 2026-10-25, legal has flagged one small consent caveat, but it should not block the extract.
- Procurement: they will want a standard vendor questionnaire + SOC2 evidence. I'll loop them if needed.

A couple of clarifications on milestones:
- For the baseline run, can we get a predefined pipeline (tokenization, normalization) so our engineers can reproduce results locally?
- For latency targets, our production SLO is 200ms p95 for the summarization endpoint; anything above that will need edge-caching or smaller model variants.

I'll confirm owners internally and circle back by EOD tomorrow.

—Alex
Senior Engineering Manager, HealthGrid

Thanks Vanessa — I reviewed the model shortlist and the bench targets with the clinical team. A few notes:

- PHI handling: we need to run an internal PHI-detection scan on the de-identified extract before sharing. I can own that and aim to finish by 2026-10-23.
- Quality metric: instead of ROUGE only, can we include a clinician-annotated binary pass/fail on a 100-sample set? That will be our tie-breaker for acceptance.
- Cost target: $0.85/1k is in the right neighborhood; if we can show the quantized RW-Instruct variant meets the clinical pass-rate, procurement is more likely to greenlight.

We'll confirm dataset timing after the PHI scan. Procurement wanted an initial cost estimate for budgeting; can Redwood provide a short cost breakdown by model variant?

Caroline

Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 13:07:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: MAP: technical evaluation slate & milestone alignment

Vanessa / team — added a quick runbook proposal as inline bullets for the baseline and tuning passes. Diego, can you confirm infra assumptions (GPU types, network egress, dataset size)?

Runbook highlights (draft):
- Baseline run: 1x A100-80GB / 2-way shard, batch-size 8, seq-length 1024 for standardization. Output token cap 256.
- Tuning pass: apply int8 quantization for RW-Instruct-13B and run latency sweep at 1k, 10k, 50k qps buckets (simulated).
- Logging: token-level latency traces + cost-per-call estimate exported to the shared Drive folder.

If HealthGrid needs lower p95 (200ms), we should plan either a smaller model or a caching front layer. That will impact the acceptance pass criteria.

Diego — I also attached a short latency/cost worksheet (latency-cost-targets.xlsx) in the MAP folder; please drop expected run hours so we can provide procurement with an initial estimate.

Thanks,
Karthik
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

Thanks all — quick alignment note after the internal confirmations I received this morning:

- Dataset & PHI scan: Caroline (HealthGrid) — due 2026-10-23
- Baseline run: Diego (Redwood SE) — due 2026-11-02
- Latency/cost tuning & quantization: Karthik (Redwood SE) — due 2026-11-09
- Clinician quality pass: Caroline + HealthGrid QA — due 2026-11-16
- Procurement & contract kick: Procurement Team (HealthGrid) + Marissa (Redwood AM) — procurement start 2026-10-25; target close for MAP: 2026-11-30

Action items for Redwood:
- Diego: confirm infra (GPU/slots) and estimated run-hours in latency-cost-targets.xlsx by EOD 2026-10-22.
- Karthik: produce a 1-page cost comparison per model variant for Procurement by 2026-10-23 (use the Drive cost sheet).
- Marissa: prepare standard SOC2 evidence and vendor PO template; drop into Drive and mark for Procurement review.

HealthGrid action items:
- Caroline: finish PHI scan and confirm dataset extract delivery date by 2026-10-23.
- Alex: confirm baseline pipeline details and whether engineering will accept Redwood's normalization steps or require a local reproducible script.
- Procurement: indicate any additional paperwork required to start the contract path.

If everyone is aligned I will update the MAP-draft-v1.pdf with the owners/timelines and move the MAP to 'in-flight' status in HubSpot. Please reply with any objections by EOD tomorrow; otherwise I'll consider these owners accepted and update the document.

Thanks — looking forward to getting the benchmark runs started.

Vanessa Ortiz
